title: Revert scope descriptor
description: From basalt_meta version 20 (owner decisions RS-1 to RS-4). What a revert covers: the binding's select and proposed, the select of POST /api/v1/reverts/{revertId}/scope, and the select that tool results show the agent. Postgres normalizes it before storing or signing it: every key present, lists sorted by their text COLLATE "C" and deduplicated, null for all, written by the text rules (CONTRACT.md, Stores, Text rules; Postgres's jsonb text follows them), so the same choice always gives the same text. The key store is reserved for multi-store work (RS-4): absent today, and Postgres refuses a descriptor that carries it (INVALID_ARGUMENT). See CONTRACT.md, Revert, The scope descriptor.

runs.description: A CHANGE or RUN is one run already: runs is only for TASK.

scopeId.description: The changeId, runId or taskId the scope names.

agents.description: Agents whose changes are in the selection, each agent:<name> (CONTRACT.md, Stores, Agent names), sorted; the guard maps each to its role. An agent's proposal names exactly one: the requesting agent. null (only in a person's widen request) means every agent with changes in the scope; Postgres stores and signs it as given, and the binding's agentRows then names each one.

runs.description: null: every run of the selected agents in the scope. Otherwise run ids, sorted, each inside the scope and of a selected agent. Only with scope TASK (a CHANGE or RUN is one run already).

resources.description: null: every resource. Otherwise resource names in the store's form, sorted, each written in the scope by a selected agent; in Postgres schema.table names, each a guarded table. Filters lines, not changes: a change that wrote two tables can be half selected.
